lessons.title: Introductions
lessons.body:
## Goal
Introduce yourself, describe your work or studies and a hobby, then answer two unexpected questions.

## Listening
Open [British Council B2 listening](https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/free-resources/listening/b2) and select **A business interview**. If unavailable, choose a comparable B2 clip. Listen without subtitles first; record the gist. Listen again for three details; check against the transcript or source afterward. Save the exact title and timestamps. If audio is unavailable, have a partner or external voice tool read an original passage and label it as such.

## Language focus: Present simple vs present perfect
Ask the mentor for two correction exercises, two transformations and one spontaneous response on this focus. Attempt before seeing answers.

## Useful chunks
- be responsible for
- have experience with
- take ownership of
- work on
- make a decision

## Speaking mission
Introduce yourself, describe your work or studies and a hobby, then answer two unexpected questions. Speak aloud without a written script; ask at least one question back. Request follow-ups one at a time. Correct up to three important issues and repeat a 60–120 second answer. The in-app mentor is text-only; use a partner, voice tool or private self-recording for actual speech.

## Pronunciation
Shadow 20–40 seconds of the listening clip, focusing on stress and thought groups.

## Session evidence
Save the listening source and actual score (if checked), speaking minutes (label estimates), confidence 1–5, up to three corrections, your own examples and the next priority. Revisit phrases after 1, 3, 7 and 14 days. Confirm tasks only after actual attempts.

documents.title: Study routine and resources
documents.body:
# Study routine
Eight weeks of speaking-first B2 practice with progression toward C1; not formal CEFR certification. Initial level must be diagnosed. Use 55 minutes on regular days, 30 on review days. Warm up 5 min, listen 12 min, language 8 min, shadow 5 min, speak 20 min and log 5 min. On short days use 5 minutes listening, 10 speaking, 5 review. Aim for 15 minutes of learner speech on full days. On review days prioritise retrieval, listening, speaking and feedback.

## Resources
- [British Council B2 listening](https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/free-resources/listening/b2)
- [British Council B2 speaking](https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/free-resources/speaking/b2)
- [BBC 6 Minute English](https://podcasts.apple.com/gb/podcast/6-minute-english/id262026947)
- [Software Engineering Radio](https://se-radio.net/)
- [CEFR spoken language criteria](https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-%203-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-qualitative-aspects-of-spoken-language-use)

External resources are linked, not reproduced. Episode themes are suggestions; check availability. Optional: English File Upper-Intermediate and English Grammar in Use (use legally acquired copies).

## Vocabulary
Use chunks in your own sentences, say them aloud, and retrieve after 1, 3, 7 and 14 days. Regular days: five chunks; review days: at most two new ones.

## Voice and privacy
The platform mentor works with text. For speech, use a conversation partner, external Voice tool or private self-recording; save only a brief nonconfidential summary. Do not assume the mentor heard audio or checked an external source. No private learner logs belong in Git.

AI-assisted curriculum; editorial review pending.

documents.title: Speaking scorecard and progress log
documents.body:
# Speaking scorecard
Use the same two-minute prompt on Days 1, 28 and 56 and add unseen questions. Checkpoints on Days 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49 and 56.

Rate each of the five dimensions in the platform from 0 to 2: 0 = not yet demonstrated or needs substantial support; 1 = partly independent; 2 = independently demonstrated for the task. This local scale is not a CEFR level or official exam result. Confidence 1–5 is separate. Leave unevaluated criteria unrated.

| Dimension | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Range | Appropriate vocabulary and varied structures |
| Accuracy | Errors do not regularly obstruct meaning |
| Fluency | Sustained spontaneous speech with manageable pauses |
| Interaction | Relevant replies, questions, clarification and repair |
| Coherence | Connected, organised ideas and clear transitions |

## Log template
- Day and date; complete or partial
- Listening title and timestamps; actual checked score or not assessed
- Speaking minutes (label estimates)
- Confidence before/after (1–5)
- Evidence for the five dimensions; pronunciation observation only if heard
- Up to three corrections and new examples
- Five chunks (review days: at most two new ones)
- Next priority and review dates +1/+3/+7/+14

## Targets
Aim to complete at least 45 sessions; speak independently for 2–3 minutes and handle three follow-ups; sustain a 15-minute everyday conversation; explain a professional decision and its trade-offs; retrieve at least 16 of 20 sampled phrases after a week. Compare actual evidence rather than claiming guaranteed C1. Adapt the difficulty based on results.

documents.title: Conversation mentor protocol
documents.body:
# Mentor protocol
Use clear natural English by default; explain in simple English or Russian if explicitly requested. Ask one question at a time; wait for an attempt before giving an answer. Use warm-up, listening recap, target language, role-play, follow-ups and a final independent retry. Encourage the learner to talk most of the time in a real voice session.

Prioritise intelligibility. Ask for self-correction first; give at most three high-value corrections, distinguishing errors from style. Avoid interrupting every mistake. Never infer accent from text, fabricate listening scores or invent personal experiences. Use fictional scenarios explicitly when needed. If listening is too hard, substitute B1 material temporarily; if easy, use unfamiliar native-speed material. Keep progress learner-confirmed. In text chat, provide prompts for speaking externally and assess only text actually supplied.

rubric.title: Range: varied and appropriate vocabulary and structures
Accuracy: grammar and vocabulary support meaning
Fluency: connected spontaneous speech with manageable pauses
Interaction: relevant responses, questions and repair
